summary: v8.4.0 round-robin/even distribution + new reaction config fields validated. All 7 backend tests pass (test_round_robin_distribution_v840.py). Auth on REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL, POST /api/tasks persistence of participant_reactions/floating_emoji/reaction_interval_min/reaction_interval_max, even distribution across 3 simulated workers, strict capacity_max=10 enforcement on /workers/me/claim, and GET /api/workers shape (capacity_max + reported_capacity) all verified.

minor.issue: Review request mentions distribution_mode='round_robin' as a task-level field but TaskCreate model (server.py:200) does NOT define it. Pydantic silently ignores the extra key — request succeeds but the value is never persisted. distribution mode is a GLOBAL backend env var (DISTRIBUTION_MODE in /app/backend/.env). If per-task distribution is intended, the field must be added to TaskCreate + TaskOut + task doc.

Current /app/backend/.env sets DISTRIBUTION_MODE="auto" (not "round_robin"). Code default if env unset is "round_robin" (server.py:881). The round-robin per-cycle wave_cap (ROUND_ROBIN_TAKE_PER_CYCLE=1) is therefore NOT active in this deployment. "auto" still does strict equal split, so even distribution works — but the visual wave pattern documented at server.py:984-994 will not appear.
No endpoint exists. Single-task read is only possible via /tasks/active or /tasks/previous list scans. Tests fall back to /tasks/active.

action_items: Decide if distribution_mode should be a per-task field (then add to TaskCreate/TaskOut + persist + read in worker_claim_tasks) OR remove the mention from the problem statement.

Optionally flip /app/backend/.env DISTRIBUTION_MODE from 'auto' to 'round_robin' if the wave-cap behaviour is the desired UX. Today the system does an EQUAL split via the 'auto' branch which is functionally correct for the 'no single worker takes everything' requirement.
Consider adding a GET /api/tasks/{task_id} endpoint for single-task reads (helps frontends + tests).
critical_code_review_comments: worker_claim_tasks (server.py:887) correctly enforces equal_share = ceil(members/online_count) when DISTRIBUTION_MODE in (auto, even, round_robin). my_already tracking via task_chunks aggregate prevents repeated polls from one worker grabbing more than fair-share — verified empirically: 3 test workers each got exactly 23 bots when 4 workers were online (90/4=22.5 -> ceil=23) instead of one greedily taking 90.

_effective_capacity (line 609) returns int(capacity_max) verbatim — strict admin policy, validated: cap=10 worker received exactly 10 bots in one claim even though reported_capacity=200 and 200 bots were pending.

TaskCreate (server.py:200) Pydantic model has NO `extra` config, so unknown fields like distribution_mode are silently dropped. Either explicitly forbid extras (extra='forbid') for clearer API errors, or add distribution_mode as a real field if per-task mode is intended.
server.py is 2118 lines — still well over the 700-line guideline. Split workers/tasks/admin/auth into separate routers.
FastAPI on_event hooks (line 2052, 2060) remain deprecated — migrate to lifespan context manager.

Pre-existing live worker named '1' (cap=80) was heartbeating during tests; round-robin algorithm correctly included it in online_count so each of our 3 test workers got fair-share=23 instead of 30. Algorithm behaves correctly under realistic mixed workload.

test_credentials: admin@finalzoom.com / Admin@FinalZoom2026 — works first try via cookie auth on https://vps-deploy-guide-3.preview.emergentagent.com.
seed_data_creation: Each test spins up TEST_-prefixed workers + a transient task via /api/tasks then deletes both in teardown (DELETE /api/workers/{id} and DELETE /api/tasks/{id}). No residue.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_round_robin_distribution_v840.py is the v8.4 regression suite. Important quirk: the deployment has a real worker '1' polling /workers/me/claim continuously, so online_count is always >= 4. The distribution test detects this and recomputes the expected fair-share = ceil(90/online_count). When no external workers are online, the test asserts the 3 test workers sum to exactly 90. DISTRIBUTION_MODE='auto' currently; for the wave-cap behaviour you must export DISTRIBUTION_MODE='round_robin' (and restart backend).
rca of the issue: Initial test failure (each worker stuck at 23 bots, total=69 of 90) was NOT a bug — it was a real online worker named '1' heartbeating during the test, making online_count=4 instead of 3. equal_share = ceil(90/4) = 23, so the algorithm correctly bounded each worker at 23. Test updated to compute expected fair-share from live online_count. Algorithm correctness is confirmed: no single-worker greed, even split per-worker, all 90 distributed across all online workers (test 3 + live 1 = 4 workers = 23+23+23+21=90).
